subject.title: [Feature]: Memory durability config — hard flush threshold, priority-aware compaction, cache TTL

question: Should OpenClaw add public config/runtime contracts for hard token memory flush, priority-preserving compaction metadata, and embedding-cache TTL, and should those three contracts be accepted together or split?
rationale: Current source lacks all three requested surfaces, but adding them changes public memory/config semantics and overlaps compaction lifecycle, memory plugin ownership, and hash-based embedding-cache behavior.

options.title: Split And Decide Each Contract
options.body: Approve, reject, or redesign hard flush, priority preservation, and TTL independently before implementation so the public config surface stays narrow.

options.title: Accept Bundled Durability Package
options.body: Treat the three knobs as one production-memory durability package and require fresh-install, upgrade, and scale proof before merge.

options.title: Defer New Config Surface
options.body: Keep current memory flush/search behavior and route remaining cache and priority work to narrower existing or future issues until maintainers explicitly accept new config.

recommendation.title: Split And Decide Each Contract
recommendation.body: Approve, reject, or redesign hard flush, priority preservation, and TTL independently before implementation so the public config surface stays narrow.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest concrete history signal for the current memory-flush runtime and related memory-core policy points to steipete.
